original_question: Given positive integers k_1, ..., k_n, does there exist a real number x such that ||k_i x|| >= 1/(n+1) for every i = 1, ..., n?
target_in_paper: In Michel Waldschmidt, Open Diophantine Problems, Section 2.2 ("Thue-Siegel-Roth-Schmidt"), the exact target is the unnumbered open question introduced as one of the "view obstruction Problems" on journal pp. 262-263.

refined_question: For every integer n >= 1 and every choice of positive integers k_1, ..., k_n, does there exist a real number x such that ||k_i x|| >= 1/(n+1) for all i = 1, ..., n, where ||t|| denotes the distance from t to the nearest integer?
justification: The draft is aiming at the exact unnumbered view-obstruction question stated in Section 2.2. Waldschmidt writes that one of the open "view obstruction Problems" asks whether, given n positive integers k_1, ..., k_n, there exists a real number x with ||k_i x|| >= 1/(n+1) for each i. The immediately preceding nearby context supplies the meaning of ||·|| as distance to the nearest integer, and the next sentence adds that 1/(n+1) is best possible in the sense that it cannot be increased. Unlike the template mentioned in your instructions, this paper does not contain a relevant Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 for this draft; the faithful target here is this unnumbered question in Section 2.2.
